config.title: forwardRef & Exposing DOM Nodes

intro.title: forwardRef & Exposing DOM Nodes
intro.body: In this lesson, you will build a simple form where you can focus a custom input field by clicking a button outside of it. You'll learn how to use the forwardRef pattern in Vue to expose a DOM node from a child component to its parent. This involves using Vue's ref system and the defineExpose macro to make internal elements accessible. By the end, you'll understand how to control DOM elements across component boundaries in a Vue application.
intro.usecase: In Vue applications, exposing DOM nodes with forwardRef is essential when building reusable form components like custom input fields, date pickers, or rich text editors. This pattern allows parent components to directly access child DOM elements to programmatically trigger focus, select text, or measure dimensions—common requirements in data-intensive dashboards and admin panels. For example, in a multi-step registration form, you might use forwardRef to automatically focus the next input field after validation, or in a financial dashboard to scroll a specific data table into view. This technique is also valuable for integrating third-party libraries that require direct DOM manipulation, such as charting tools or drag-and-drop interfaces.

objectives: Implement a forwardRef to pass a DOM reference from a child component to its parent
Apply the ref attribute to bind a DOM element within a child component
Expose DOM nodes from a child component using the defineExpose function
Manipulate DOM elements in the parent component using references obtained via forwardRef
Configure a child component to expose specific DOM nodes for parent access
Integrate forwardRef with template refs to control focus on input elements
Construct a form validation scenario where parent components access child DOM nodes

steps.title: Bind ref to input element using v-bind
steps.instruction: In the ChildComponent template, bind the forwarded ref prop to the input element's ref attribute using v-bind.
steps.hint: Use v-bind (or the shorthand :) to connect the ref prop to the input's ref attribute.
steps.analogousExample:
// Binding a prop to an element attribute
<template>
  <input :ref="forwardedRef" />
</template>
steps.expectedOutcome: The input element in ChildComponent will have its ref attribute bound to the forwardedRef prop, allowing the parent to access the input's DOM node.
successCriteria: The ChildComponent template includes an input element with :ref="forwardedRef" binding.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure you're using v-bind (or :) to bind the forwardedRef prop to the input's ref attribute.
steps.feedbackWrong: The input element needs to have its ref attribute bound to the forwardedRef prop using v-bind syntax.

steps.title: Add child component to parent template with ref binding
steps.instruction: In the ParentComponent's template, add the ChildComponent and bind the parent's ref to the forwardedRef prop.
steps.hint: Use the child component's tag name and bind the ref using v-bind or the colon shorthand.
steps.analogousExample:

</template>
steps.expectedOutcome: The parent component's template includes the child component with the ref properly passed as a prop.
